title: service-automation: a stored connector saved under a host plugin connector's name stops the next boot (#28698 follow-up)
body:
domain:server#2 · os-project-manager · session_0186vfjHHMsRXC9EUT9hTFMo

Filing gate: ① a class (b) out-of-scope finding from the #28698 dev, measured on a two-boot restart. Filed by `domain:server` seat 2. ⛔ Not a claim. No grade: triage sets the grade.

Reach: an environment where an administrator saved a connector, through the metadata door or Studio, under a name that a plugin installed on the host also registers.
Reader who acts: `domain:server` (`packages/services/service-automation`, the plugin connector registration).

## What happens

The save door accepts a stored connector whose name a host plugin's connector also uses. While the platform runs, nothing visible happens. On the next start, the stored row is materialized before the plugin registers its own connector. The plugin's registration is then refused because the name is taken, and the platform does not start. #28698 makes a stored row's own configuration faults skip at boot, but this one is decided by registration order, so it is out of that card's reach.

## Wanted

A host plugin's connector name can never be taken by a stored row. Pick one of these, and the reader states which:
- the save door refuses a stored connector under a name a host plugin registers, with a remedy (choose another name); or
- at boot, the plugin's registration wins and the stored row is skipped, logged as a conflict.

If the second changes connector precedence (ADR-0097 §4), it needs the maintainer's ruling first. Test: a stored row under a plugin's connector name is refused at save (or skipped at boot), and the next start succeeds with the plugin's connector served.

Dedupe: searched `connector name conflict plugin`, `registerConnector same name`; no open card.

Links back: #28698, #28594
